name: Schotten Totten: Five Stones
summary: Two players take turns placing cards from a private hand onto their side of five Stones, forming three-card poker-like formations; a player claims a Stone with the stronger side, and the first to claim 3 of the 5 Stones wins.

player.meaning: The card codes this player holds, like 'R7'. Only the owner sees them.
Number of Stones this player has claimed. This is the score.
'A' for seat 1 or 'B' for seat 2. A acts in odd rounds and B in even rounds.

game.initial: all 36 codes R1..R9, B1..B9, G1..G9, Y1..Y9

game.meaning: Number of cards left in the draw pile. It is 24 after the deal.
1 (A) in odd rounds and 2 (B) in even rounds.
Face-up cards on A's side of Stone 1, at most 3.
Face-up cards on B's side of Stone 1, at most 3.
Who has claimed each Stone 1-5: '' (unclaimed), 'A' or 'B'.
For each Stone, 'A' or 'B': the player who first completed 3 cards on their side while the other side held fewer than 3.

setup: The deck holds the 36 cards R1-R9, B1-B9, G1-G9 and Y1-Y9.
Seats are assigned at random: seat 1 is Player A (role 'A') and seat 2 is Player B (role 'B'). A takes the first turn.
Each player is dealt 6 cards: each draw picks a random card from deck, appends it to that player's hand and removes it from deck.
All ten Stone sides start empty. stone_owner and first_finisher start as five empty entries.

round.effect: round += 1; active_seat = 1 if round is odd, else 2.
Announce every Stone's sides (stone_k_a, stone_k_b), stone_owner, each player's claimed, and deck_count.
Each player privately sees their own hand.

round.answer: one card code from their hand
round.effect: The chosen card is remembered as the card to play.

round.answer: one Stone number from 1-5 that is unclaimed (stone_owner[k] == '') and where the active player's side holds fewer than 3 cards
round.effect: The chosen Stone k is remembered.
Remove the chosen card from the active player's hand and append it to stone_k_a (if active_seat == 1) or stone_k_b (if active_seat == 2). Cards never move again.
If the active side of Stone k now has 3 cards and the opposite side has fewer than 3, set first_finisher[k] = the active player's role.
If deck_count > 0, draw a random card from deck into the active player's hand and set deck_count -= 1.

For each Stone k = 1..5 where stone_owner[k] == '' and both len(stone_k_a) == 3 and len(stone_k_b) == 3, compute strength_a and strength_b by the strength formula. If strength_a > strength_b, the owner is 'A'. If strength_b > strength_a, the owner is 'B'. If they are equal, the owner is first_finisher[k]. Set stone_owner[k] to the owner and add 1 to that player's claimed. Announce the result.
End the game if any player's claimed >= 3, or if round >= 30. Otherwise continue.

ending.condition: max over players of claimed >= 3, or round >= 30
ending.decided_by: A player's standing is the number of Stones they have claimed. The first to reach 3 wins at once. If round 30 ends without that, the player with more claimed Stones wins, and equal counts share the win (a draw).

rules.text: When the game starts, each player holds 6 cards in hand and the deck holds 24.
When the round number is odd, seat 1 (A) is the only player asked to act; when it is even, seat 2 (B) is the only one asked.
When the active player is asked for a card, the options are exactly the cards in their hand.
When the active player is asked for a Stone, the options are exactly the Stones that are unclaimed and whose side for that player holds fewer than 3 cards.
When a card is played on Stone k, it leaves the player's hand, is appended to that player's side of Stone k, and never moves again.
When a played card is the third on its side and the other side holds fewer than 3 cards, first_finisher[k] is set to the player's role.
When deck_count > 0 after a play, the active player draws one card and deck_count drops by 1; when deck_count == 0, no card is drawn.
When all three cards on a side share a colour, have different values, and highest minus lowest is 2, the strength is the sum of the values + 120 (for example, R3 R4 R5 has strength 132).
When all three values on a side are equal, the strength is the sum + 90 (for example, R7 B7 G7 has strength 111).
When all three cards share a colour but the side is not a straight flush, the strength is the sum + 60 (for example, B1 B5 B9 has strength 75).
When the values are all different with highest minus lowest equal to 2 but the colours are mixed, the strength is the sum + 30 (for example, R6 B7 G8 has strength 51).
When a side has no formation, its strength is just the sum (for example, R2 B5 G9 has strength 16).
When both sides of an unclaimed Stone hold 3 cards, the side with the higher strength claims it and that player's claimed goes up by 1.
When both sides of a completed Stone have equal strength, the Stone's first_finisher claims it.
When a Stone is claimed, it can no longer be offered as a Stone to play on.
When a player's claimed reaches 3, the game ends immediately and that player wins.
When round 30 ends and nobody has 3 Stones, the player with more claimed Stones wins, and equal counts are a draw.

offers.question: Which card to play
offers.who: the active seat only (seat 1 in odd rounds, seat 2 in even rounds)
offers.options: Every card code currently in that seat's hand. The inactive seat is asked nothing.

offers.question: Which Stone to play on
offers.options: Every Stone number 1-5 with stone_owner[k] == '' whose side for the active player holds fewer than 3 cards. Claimed Stones and Stones where the player's side is full are never offered.

choices.why: The designer fixed the game at 2. Each Stone has exactly two sides, A and B, so the game does not scale to more seats.
The rules include no table talk. This is a two-player positional duel, and messages would add nothing the rules call for.

choices.what: Card choice and Stone choice are two sequential asks
choices.why: The source lists them as separate steps (2) and (3). Asking them separately keeps each option list exact.

choices.what: Drawing the top card is a random pick from deck
choices.why: The deck is shuffled, so a random draw is equivalent to taking the top card.

choices.what: The round counter and active seat are updated at the start of each round
choices.why: This lets the engine pick the active player by arithmetic on round parity.

choices.what: The end check also fires at round >= 30
choices.why: The source caps the game at 30 rounds. At that point all 30 slots are filled and every Stone has been resolved.

Each card commits to one Stone permanently. A thoughtful player judges which formations are still possible given the visible cards, decides which Stones to contest and which to concede, and races to finish a side first so they win ties.

simplifications.what: Stone sides are table attributes (stone_k_a and stone_k_b) rather than per-player lists
simplifications.why: The engine has no player-attribute operand for comparison. Keeping both sides on the table lets resolution compare the two strengths directly.

simplifications.what: Strength is computed by calculating each card's colour (first letter) and value (digit) inside the resolution update
simplifications.why: The engine has no lookup operation. The formation test is pure arithmetic on the three values and colours, so no referee is needed.

simplifications.what: All five Stones are resolved in one update step, using per-Stone conditional operations
simplifications.why: Each Stone's resolution is an independent conditional update. No branching block of steps is needed.
